transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-19 16:00 UTC / 45m / Recording available
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Ravi Menon (Redwood SE), Li Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (NovaBio CTO), Ben Carter (Infra Engineer), Marta Silva (Security Lead), Diego Alvarez (Dev Lead)
---
[00:00] Jamie (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, we set aside 45 minutes, the plan is quick intro, understand your current infra and constraints, then Ravi and Li will cover the private deployment options and networking. quick yes if that works
[00:15] Aisha (NovaBio CTO): yes that works thanks jamie. we're looking at private deployment options, big priority is data residency and not sending PHI to public endpoints.
[00:30] Jamie: got it, that's common. can you give us the quick stack and where you're running most workloads?
[00:40] Ben (Infra): we run primarily in us-east-1 for the model training and us-west-2 for the app tier, our medical imaging processing lives in a dedicated VPC in us-east-1. we'd like inference close to the data to minimize egress and latency.
[00:55] Ravi (Redwood SE): okay so region constraints matter. Redwood Private supports VPC peering and private endpoints for the control plane; you can also do an on-prem air-gapped option but sounds like VPC peering or PrivateLink will be the right fit. question: do you have a central shared services VPC or per-environment VPCs?
[01:15] Ben: we have a hub-and-spoke model, shared-services in us-east-1, spoke VPCs for prod/dev. we prefer peering to the shared-services VPC, we avoid transitive peering where possible.
[01:30] Li (Redwood SE): noted. just to call out—our recommended pattern is either VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink endpoints depending on whether you need cross-AZ traffic and how you want routing. peering is straightforward but requires route table updates; PrivateLink gives more control and avoids route table changes but is regional per NLB.
[01:55] Marta (Security): can you confirm how secrets and keys are managed? we require KMS integration and we need to ensure that Redwood can't access plaintext model inputs.
[02:05] Ravi: yes we integrate with customer KMS—customer-managed keys (CMKs) for at-rest encryption. for control plane metadata we provide options for customer key wrapping for secrets. note: some audit logs and metrics (anonymized) may be stored in Redwood's control plane unless you choose the private control plane option which we can deploy into your VPC.
[02:30] Aisha: private control plane? please expand.
[02:35] Jamie: sure. Redwood Private can be deployed with a customer-managed control plane that sits in your VPC or VPCs, so the management traffic never leaves your network. that option is more common for regulated workloads and we have customers running it in multiple regions.
[02:55] Diego (Dev Lead): latency wise if we keep models in us-east-1 and our app is in us-west-2, what are we looking at?
[03:05] Ravi: cross-region will add RTT; best practice is colocation—either move inference to us-west-2 or replicate the model to us-east-1. when using dedicated capacity we can pin GPUs in specific regions. typical added latency for a cross-region call is 50-120ms depending on service mesh, but token generation also depends on model size and prompt length.
[03:30] Ben: we care about egress costs — if inference runs in a different region it will cost us. any way to reduce that?
[03:40] Li: yes, keep inference close to the data or use VPC peering inside the same region—no cross-region egress. also we support prefix/KV caching which can reduce repeat-run traffic for similar prompts.
[03:55] Marta: compliance — we need SOC2 type II, ISO 27001, and audit logs for all admin actions. is that included?
[04:05] Jamie: we have SOC2 and ISO artifacts, and we can share our compliance pack. for Private deployments we can also enable audit logging to your own logging cluster via an encrypted stream. we'll include the SOC2 report in the security pack.
[04:25] Aisha: for VPC peering there are often CIDR overlap issues. what are your constraints?
[04:30] Ravi: peering requires non-overlapping CIDR. if you have overlap we recommend PrivateLink or a transitGateway pattern. we can also use NAT+proxying inside your network but that's more complex.
[04:50] Diego: what's the typical network port/endpoint pattern? do we open ports outbound to Redwood or inbound?
[04:58] Li: with VPC peering you route to our service endpoints in our VPC, so traffic is within the AWS backbone. with PrivateLink you create an endpoint service backed by NLB — essentially you create an Interface Endpoint in your VPC that talks to our NLB in our service VPC. for Private control plane you can run the control plane subnets inside your VPC and we provide helm charts / terraform.
[05:25] Ben: any firewall or security groups specifics?
[05:30] Ravi: we recommend least-privilege security groups: allow only your app subnets to the Redwood subnets or endpoint ENIs. we'll provide recommended SG and route table entries in the runbook.
[05:45] [06:00] Jamie: i'd like to surface cost tradeoffs—dedicated reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated) gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost, but requires capacity commits. hosted with private endpoints can be pay-as-you-go but higher per-token. for heavy throughput, Dedicated often wins.
[06:20] Aisha: we're not sure of expected token volume yet, but we expect bursts during batch inference; can you do autoscaling?
[06:30] Ravi: yes Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst capacity. for the private deployment we can tie autoscaler to your metrics and scale GPU pools. note that scaling GPU capacity has startup time depending on instance warm-up — we'll size for headroom.
[06:55] Marta: data residency — we need logs and raw inputs to never leave region. is that possible?
[07:05] Li: yes. you can choose region-specific deployments and we support local-only storage. for extra isolation we can deploy the private control plane into your regional VPC so telemetry and logs stay inside the region.
[07:25] Diego: what about SSO and RBAC? we use Okta.
[07:30] Jamie: we support SAML/SSO (Okta) and granular RBAC. for Private deployments you can federate against your IdP and sync group mappings.
[07:45] Ben: any network prerequisites we should prepare?
[07:50] Ravi: we'll need your VPC CIDR(s), the subnets for the endpoint, security group rules, NAT/IGW layout if outbound access needed, and whether you allow cross-account peering. also confirm whether you prefer PrivateLink or peering.
[08:10] Aisha: we prefer PrivateLink in prod as it minimizes route table changes and we can control endpoints per VPC. dev can do peering.
[08:20] Jamie: noted. do you have any procurement or contract timing constraints?
[08:25] Aisha: we'd like to pilot before end of quarter, need vendor security review completed, and pricing to be inside a 60 day approval window.
[08:35] Jamie: good. we'll get the security pack today and aim to have a pilot proposal and costs by end of next week.
[08:45] Ravi: technical question — model weights. do you plan to bring-your-own-model or use Redwood-curated models?
[08:55] Diego: we plan to use an internal fine-tuned model containing PHI'd training signals; we need to control where weights are stored.
[09:05] Li: fine — we support customer-hosted model artifacts in S3 buckets under your account with IAM roles; we can mount that into the inference nodes or have the runtime pull from your S3 via a role. that keeps weights in your control.
[09:25] Marta: so who has access to encryption keys?
[09:30] Ravi: customer KMS CMK, and access only via roles you grant. we don't hold plaintext keys. admin ops that require access can be scoped via IAM and audit logged.
[09:45] Aisha: can you do a network test or a small latency benchmark during pilot?
[09:50] Jamie: yes we'll propose a short benchmark run — typically we ask for a small test dataset, model size, and expected qps. we can run a 24-72 hour benchmark to show p95 latency and cost.
[10:05] Ben: ok great. what's required to run that benchmark?
[10:10] Ravi: network-wise we need your endpoint (if PrivateLink, interface endpoint DNS), sample traffic pattern, and any auth tokens. we prefer to run inside your VPC so results reflect real network conditions.
[10:25] Diego: one more — do you support transit gateway peering if we want centralization?
[10:30] Li: yes TransitGateway is supported and often used for multi-account hub-and-spoke. we'll include a transit gateway diagram in the runbook.
[10:45] Marta: are there any known gotchas with AWS PrivateLink for large model payloads?
[10:50] Ravi: PrivateLink has ENI and throughput limits per ENI; for high throughput we recommend multiple interfaces and load-balancer capacity, or use a dedicated VPC with direct peering if you need very high sustained bandwidth. we'll size based on your qps and average token size.
[11:10] Jamie: i'd like to summarize actions and timeline before we close.
[11:15] Jamie: action items: we'll send security pack + compliance docs, runbook with peering and PrivateLink patterns, sample terraform, and a pilot proposal with pricing. Ben will share VPC CIDRs and preferred region, Ravi will prepare a network diagram. schedule technical deep dive for 10/22. agreed?
[11:35] Aisha: yes agreed. thanks everyone.
[11:40] Jamie: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with links to the docs and a calendar invite for 10/22.
